prompt:
Bug report: cooking bechamel today took the new milk (lot HD-1026) although lot HD-1022 expires tomorrow. Fix it and add a regression test.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Fixed. `consumptionOrder` in src/domain/batches.js sorted batches newest-received first, so stock was used last-in, first-out. It now follows the FEFO rule in docs/DATA.md: the batch that expires first goes first, batches with no expiry go last, and ties go to the one received first, then the lower id. I added two regression tests to tests/stock.test.js: cooking bechamel now takes its milk from HD-1022 (batch 4), and a second test checks the full ordering rule. Both new tests fail on the old code. With the fix, `npm test` passes (28/28) and `npm run lint` passes. I also added a changelog bullet.

check.why: FEFO by the data rules, with a regression test
